fr.recommendations:
• Install a clearly visible address marker at the driveway entrance that can be read from the road in both directions.
• Mark the access drive entry with reflective posts or markers to help responders locate the property quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and prevent branches from blocking emergency vehicles.
• Post a property map or diagram at the driveway entrance identifying the main residence, detached structure, and equipment storage area.
• Clearly mark all access points to both structures so responders can locate them without searching.
• Keep the equipment storage area clear of items that would block vehicle movement or responder access around the structures.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure to allow responders to move freely between buildings.
• Mark any rear access points clearly from both inside and outside the perimeter fencing.
• Keep gates in perimeter fencing unlocked or secured with a Knox box or standardized lock responders can open without delay.
• Identify and mark the primary and alternate routes between the two structures so responders can move directly without navigating around obstacles.
• Keep the parking area clear enough for emergency vehicles to stage without blocking the access drive.
• Trim vegetation along perimeter fencing lines so responders can see and reach fence access points quickly.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on scattered trees that are closest to the structure to increase separation between the tree canopy and the roofline.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to open up space between individual trees.
• Remove or cut back shrubs that are growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Mow or cut grass around the structure and any outbuildings, keeping it short during dry periods.
• Keep all access routes clear of low-hanging branches that could block a vehicle or slow emergency access.
• Remove dead or dry grass and plant material that has accumulated along the edges of the driveway.
• Maintain the existing open areas between vegetation and the structure by preventing shrubs or trees from spreading into those spaces over time.
